en.name: Hijiki, dried
en.summary: Dried hijiki keeps 6–12 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard, and 12–18 months sealed in the fridge once the bag is open. The storage conditions are published guidance for dried goods generally; no agency gives a hijiki-specific number, so read the range as a careful reading of that rule.
en.pantry: Keep it tightly sealed, away from heat, direct sunlight and damp — those are the published conditions for dried goods, and they are the whole of the method. On that basis 6–12 months is a conservative working life for a sealed bag in a cool dark cupboard. What actually ends a bag is humidity: hijiki is black, brittle and very absorbent, and once it softens in the bag it will clump and then mould. Keep the desiccant sachet in with it, squeeze the air out each time, and store the bag well away from the hob.
en.fridge: In a humid climate, sealed in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, opened hijiki keeps 12–18 months. Use a jar with a gasket or a double-bagged pack, because dried seaweed takes up fridge odours with enthusiasm. Rehydrated hijiki is a different food and a fresh one: drain it, refrigerate it, and use it within a day or two. The soaking water is discarded rather than used as stock — hijiki is high in inorganic arsenic, and several food agencies advise soaking, throwing the water away, and eating it in moderation rather than daily.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for dried hijiki and freezing the dry product gains very little, since a sealed bag is already stable for months and its enemy is moisture rather than time. Cooked hijiki dishes such as 羊栖菜の煮物 do freeze well in portions, which is the more useful thing to know; treat those as a cooked side dish rather than as this dried ingredient.
spoilage: Musty or mouldy smell when the bag is opened.
Strands that feel soft, damp or rubbery instead of brittle.
Clumping into a solid mass, or visible white or green mould.
A strong fishy or sour smell after rehydrating — discard the batch.
tips: Keep the desiccant sachet in the bag and squeeze the air out after each use.
Soak in plenty of cold water and discard the soaking water rather than using it.
Buy small bags; hijiki is used a spoonful at a time.
Store the jar away from the hob and out of the light.

faq.q: How long does dried hijiki keep?
faq.a: 6–12 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard, or 12–18 months sealed in the fridge once opened. Those ranges are a conservative reading of general dried-goods guidance, not a hijiki-specific published figure.
Only briefly. Drain it, refrigerate it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and use it within a day or two — it is a fresh food once rehydrated.

faq.q: Should the soaking water be used?
faq.a: No. Discard it. Hijiki is high in inorganic arsenic, and the standard advice is to soak, throw the water away, and eat it in moderation.

zh.name: 乾燥羊栖菜
zh.summary: 乾燥羊栖菜密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月，開封後密封冷藏約 12～18 個月。要說明的是，公布的內容是乾貨的保存條件，並沒有針對羊栖菜給出的數字，所以請把這個範圍當成對那條規則的保守解讀。
zh.pantry: 確實密封，避開高溫、陽光直射與潮濕——這就是官方對乾貨給的條件，也是這件事的全部方法。以此為基礎，密封袋放陰涼暗處約 6～12 個月是保守而合理的期限。真正毀掉一包羊栖菜的是濕氣：它黑、脆、非常吸水，一旦在袋子裡變軟就會結塊，接著長霉。乾燥劑留在袋子裡，每次用完把空氣擠掉，袋子也要放得離爐台遠一點。
zh.fridge: 在潮濕的氣候下，開封後密封放 4 °C 以下冷藏，約可放 12～18 個月。請用有膠條的密封罐或雙層袋，因為乾燥海藻吸冰箱味道的能力非常驚人。泡開後的羊栖菜是另一種食物，而且是新鮮食物：瀝乾、冷藏，並在一兩天內用完。泡的水要倒掉、不要當高湯——羊栖菜的無機砷含量偏高，多個食品機關的建議都是泡發、倒掉泡過的水、並適量食用而不是天天吃。
zh.freezer: 乾燥羊栖菜沒有公布的冷凍期限，而且把乾貨冷凍的好處很小：密封的袋子本來就能穩定放好幾個月，它的敵人是水氣而不是時間。比較實用的是：煮好的羊栖菜煮物很適合分小份冷凍——但那要當成一道熟的配菜來看，而不是當成這項乾貨。
spoilage: 打開袋子聞到霉味或土味。
海藻條摸起來軟、潮或有橡膠感，而不是脆的。
結成一整塊，或看得到白色、綠色霉斑。
泡發後有強烈腥味或酸味，整批丟掉。
tips: 乾燥劑留在袋內，每次用完把空氣擠掉。
用大量冷水泡發，泡過的水倒掉，不要拿來煮。
買小包，羊栖菜一次只用一小匙。
罐子遠離爐台、避免光照。

faq.q: 乾燥羊栖菜可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封放陰涼暗處約 6～12 個月，開封後密封冷藏約 12～18 個月。這個範圍是對乾貨通則的保守解讀，不是羊栖菜專屬的公布數字。

faq.q: 泡開的羊栖菜可以放嗎？
faq.a: 只能很短。瀝乾後放 4 °C 以下冷藏，一兩天內用完，泡發後它就是新鮮食物。

faq.q: 泡羊栖菜的水可以用嗎？
faq.a: 不要用，請倒掉。羊栖菜的無機砷偏高，標準建議是泡發、倒掉泡水、適量食用。
